The successful candidate will work with design teams and scientific collaborations in the development of high-performance digital processors for a variety of projects, including the ATLAS Experiment at [Location masked], Cosmic Microwave Background Experiments, the DUNE experiment, rare muon decay experiments (mu to e), Quantum Information Systems, and other areas. [Company name masked] is a multidisciplinary national laboratory and offers an exciting campus atmosphere in which to collaborate on interdisciplinary projects, at both the national and international levels.
cond_0236.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
PhD degree in electrical engineering, computer science, computer engineering, data science, high energy physics, or a related discipline, with up to 3 years of demonstrated expertise in a relevant research or engineering context
Deep knowledge of FPGA programming languages (VHDL or Verilog)
Strong command of C, C++, Python, or another scientific programming language
Preferred Requirements
Proven track record designing applications that use high-performance FPGAs
Substantial expertise in high-performance digital or data processing systems
Advanced knowledge of one or more of the following: embedded processors, high-speed transceivers, and optical links
Openings are available immediately; there is flexibility in starting dates for highly qualified candidates. In addition to applying online, applicants should send their curriculum vitae, a description of research interests through the application system and arrange for three letters of recommendation to hep_letters@anl.gov. For further information, contact Alexander Paramonov at aparamonov@anl.gov. Review of applications will begin once the application is completed and will continue until the positions are filled.

The successful candidate will work with design teams and scientific collaborations in the development of high-performance digital processors for a variety of projects, including the ATLAS Experiment at [Location masked], Cosmic Microwave Background Experiments, the DUNE experiment, rare muon decay experiments (mu to e), Quantum Information Systems, and other areas. [Company name masked] is a multidisciplinary national laboratory and offers an exciting campus atmosphere in which to collaborate on interdisciplinary projects, at both the national and international levels. People who do well in this role are often quick to grasp the logic of high-performance digital systems and detector readout work.
cond_0346.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
PhD degree in electrical engineering, computer science, computer engineering, data science, high energy physics, or a related discipline with 0 to 3 years of experience or equivalent
Experience with FPGA programming languages (VHDL or Verilog)
Preferred Requirements
Experience with designing applications that use high-performance FPGAs
Programming expertise in C, C++, Python, or another scientific programming language
Experience with high-performance digital or data processing systems
Experience with one or more of the following: embedded processors, high-speed transceivers, and optical links
Openings are available immediately; there is flexibility in starting dates for highly qualified candidates. In addition to applying online, applicants should send their curriculum vitae, a description of research interests through the application system and arrange for three letters of recommendation to hep_letters@anl.gov. The successful candidate will work with design teams and scientific collaborations in the development of high-performance digital processors for a variety of projects, including the ATLAS Experiment at [Location masked], Cosmic Microwave Background Experiments, the DUNE experiment, rare muon decay experiments (mu to e), Quantum Information Systems, and other areas. [Company name masked] is a multidisciplinary national laboratory and offers an exciting campus atmosphere in which to collaborate on interdisciplinary projects, at both the national and international levels. People who do well in this role are often quick to grasp the logic of high-performance digital systems and detector readout work.
cond_0517.requirements:
The candidates must have received a PhD degree in electrical engineering, computer science, computer engineering, data science, high energy physics, or a related discipline with 0 to 3 years of experience or equivalent
Experience with designing applications that use high performance FPGAs is highly desirable
Experience with FPGA programming languages (vhdl or verilog) is required
Programming expertise in C, C++, Python, or another scientific programming language is highly desirable
Experience with high-performance digital or data processing systems is desirable
Experience with one or more of the following is desirable: embedded processors, high-speed transceivers, and optical links
cond_0517.encouragement_text: Important: Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply.
cond_0517.workplace_support: We aim to support employees across different life and career stages through development resources, workplace flexibility, and inclusive benefits that make it easier to grow, contribute, and stay well.

cond_0644.intro: The High Energy Physics (HEP) Division at [Company name masked] invites applications for a postdoctoral research associate position to work in the HEP Electronics Group to develop novel instrumentation and readout systems for innovative and leading-edge detectors and other scientific research. The successful candidate will work with design teams and scientific collaborations in the development of high-performance digital processors for a variety of projects, including the ATLAS Experiment at [Location masked], Cosmic Microwave Background Experiments, the DUNE experiment, rare muon decay experiments (mu to e), Quantum Information Systems, and other areas.
